This page draws Figure 2 from the analysis datasets prepared in [Data and measures](01_data_and_measures.qmd), together with the supplied drawing coordinates.

# Four layers of one classroom


Figure 2 shows, in one small classroom (9 children), the four networks the analysis combines:

- **A. Friendship**: who named whom as a best friend. Green arrows are mutual friendships; blue arrows are one-sided.
- **B. Popularity** and **C. non-popularity**: who named whom as popular or as not popular. Social Rank is computed from these two layers.
- **D. Tokens**: every transfer in the game, darker for more tokens.

The same child keeps the same position in all four layers, so one can follow how a child who is central in one layer fares in the others.

## The assembled figure

The published figure shows the same four layers as tilted planes stacked on top of each other, with one legend. The node positions are the ones chosen for that drawing (`data/raw/figure2_layout.csv`); they are a drawing choice and play no role in any calculation. Each plane is the layout stretched, flattened and slanted.

```{r sociogram-assembled-layout}
#| code-summary: "sociogram-assembled-layout"
```

Nodes and arrows of the four planes. Mutual friendships are drawn once, with two heads.
